findings.title: NFR restated with target, boundaries and dependency direction correct
findings.description: The slice correctly restates the parent architecture NFR — Tier 2 = 60 TPS at N=50k on CUDA — naming `140-arch.simulation-scaling.md` and giving the gate a specific number (≥100 TPS, with the 1.67× headroom rationale tied to slice 146 and Tier 3 load). It also respects the architecture's explicit exemption for the fused tick: no changes to `TickResult` / world-server interface, no `SpatialQuery`/`BulkForce` involvement, no per-substrate (Metal) code paths, and `dependencies: [145]` / `interfaces: [146]` point in the correct direction (149 consumes 145's kernel, 146 consumes 149's transport-neutral API). The declared "no structural change to `build_spatial_hash`" intent is consistent with the code, where `build_spatial_hash` reads `state.cell_size` and the grid dims rather than deriving them.

findings.title: Gate configuration resolves to a workload whose N is 100,000, not 50k
findings.description: `Default bench config for gate runs: mid-flock-50k workload, S=3, max_neighbors=32` is the config that A2 (≥5× `force_total`) and A3 (≥100 TPS at N=50k) are measured on — and A3 is the stated NFR gate. But `bench/workloads/mid-flock-50k.yaml` declares `n: 100000` with `world_size: [1536.0, 1536.0]`, while its own description claims the N=50k operating point and slice 145's recorded 38 TPS at N=50k corresponds to a 756×756 world. As written, the design's gate would be evaluated at N=100k against a denominator recorded at N=50k, so the pass/fail meaning of A2/A3 is undefined. The slice must state the exact workload file (or N and world size) used for both the denominator and the gate, and either fix or disambiguate `mid-flock-50k.yaml`.

findings.title: Verification walkthrough cites a non-existent harness and unreproducible ablations
findings.description: Every command in Steps 2, 3 and 5 invokes `python scripts/bench.py --backend quadrants-fused --config <name> --N <n> --ticks <n> --subdivision-factor <S> --parity-check numpy`. There is no `scripts/bench.py` (the scripts directory contains only `148_measure_cell_occupancy.py` and `148_smem_vs_dram_microbench.py`), and the real harness is `python -m migratory.bench.cli`, whose flags are `--workload`, `--backend`, `--workload-dir`, `--results-dir`, `--list-*` — none of `--config`, `-N`, `--ticks`, `--subdivision-factor`, or `--parity-check` exist. Worse, the four Step-3 configurations meant to isolate each intervention are not distinguishable: the "Baseline (S=1, counter-gating)" and "Early exit only (S=1, break enabled)" command lines are byte-identical, as are "Cell subdivision only (S=3, counter-gating)" and "Both interventions (S=3, break enabled)". Since the break is compiled into the kernel (not behind a flag), the counter-gating rows cannot be produced on this branch at all — which is also why the task list instructs taking the baseline from `main` instead. The design needs to name the real harness/flag it will add for `subdivision_factor`, and to state explicitly which gate comparisons are against a recorded slice-145 baseline rather than a same-branch ablation. The gap left unmet is a reproducible measurement path for A2/A3.

findings.title: Component-interaction diagram misplaces the state it modifies and names a type that does not exist
findings.description: The design says `build_spatial_hash` (lines 411–462) "computes `grid_w` and `grid_h`" and that `QuadrantsFusedBackend.setup()` "stores grid_w, grid_h, cell_size, S". In the code, `build_spatial_hash` only orchestrates the four kernels plus the CPU `np.cumsum` and holds no such state; `grid_w`, `grid_h`, `n_cells` and `cell_size` are computed and stored in `GpuAgentState.setup()`, and the backend merely forwards `state.cell_size` / `state.grid_w` / `state.grid_h` into the kernel launch. The diagram's `BenchConfig` node likewise names no existing type — the actual config surface is `Workload` (YAML schema in `bench/workloads/*.yaml`) plus the module constant `DEFAULT_CELL_SIZE_MULTIPLIER`, which the design's line-80 claim ("only the cell_size value changes") does not reconcile with the task-level instruction to remove that constant. For an implementer wiring S through, the ownership of the new field is the core question and the document points at the wrong modules; the design should name `Workload`, `GpuAgentState`, and both kernel call sites (`QuadrantsFusedTickRunner.tick_once` and the `run_fused_tick` wrapper).

findings.title: "A7 seam preserved" overstates what the count-based break leaves intact
findings.description: The plan entry says both interventions use the `getNeighbors` seam, and the design concludes "A7 seam preserved: the `get_neighbors_first_k` swap point … remains intact." Two things undercut that claim. (1) The break is placed in the caller, before the seam, on a pure count condition (`k_found >= max_neighbors`), so the seam can no longer be swapped in isolation to obtain distance-ranked selection: a distance-ranked policy must keep scanning to prove no closer candidate remains, which requires changing the caller's break condition, not just the seam body — i.e. the seam is no longer the whole swap point. (2) The text says "The seam becomes unreachable when the break fires," which is not what the sketch does: the break fires only once the cap is reached, so on every pre-cap iteration the seam is still executed and now always returns accept — leaving its counter-gating branch as dead, misleading logic that the design never says to remove or mark. Either state the seam's narrowed contract explicitly (count-only break, distance-ranked requires a caller-side change) or move the gating decision so A7 stays a single-function swap.

findings.title: Benchmark target named by the slice plan (max_neighbors=7) is dropped
findings.description: The slice plan entry for (149) states: "real starling murmurations interact with ~7 nearest neighbors; `max_neighbors=32` is an intentional physics stress; the 7-neighbor operating point is a benchmark target," and the design's own source analysis notes that early-exit gain scales inversely with `max_neighbors` ("The 7-neighbor target is a meaningful operating point to benchmark at"). The design fixes every gate, criterion and walkthrough run at `max_neighbors=32` and never measures the lower-k operating point, so the regime with the largest predicted payoff relative to the 45,000-candidate scan is left unquantified and the plan's stated benchmark target has no corresponding deliverable. Deferring it is a scope reduction that should be stated and justified rather than silently omitted.

findings.title: "CPU fallback" does not exist for this backend and conflicts with the architecture's substrate posture
findings.description: "A1 and A4 can be verified on Mac (Metal or CPU fallback)" implies a CPU path for `quadrants-fused`. There is none: the backend selects CUDA on Linux and Metal on Darwin and raises on anything else, with no silent CPU degradation. The parent architecture further demotes Metal to best-effort / not gated. Rewording as "Mac/Metal for A1 and A4, CUDA-only for A2/A3/A5" would keep the verification matrix accurate and avoid implying a platform that the design does not support.

findings.title: Intervention-composition arithmetic contradicts the cited source measurements
findings.description: The composition paragraph says "With S=3 alone: candidates loaded drops to ~5000" and "With both: candidates loaded ~555," but per-cell occupancy (~555) is not the candidate count: at S=3 the scan is 7×7 cells × ~555 agents ≈ 27,000 candidates (the figure the cited slice-148 re-diagnosis itself gives). The ~5000/~555 figures conflate per-cell occupancy with candidates scanned, weakening the quantitative justification for calling the two interventions multiplicative. Aligning these numbers with the source measurements would make the expected-gain argument checkable.

findings.title: No failure-mode statement for the spatial-build cost growth at S>1
findings.description: The design states no structural change is needed for `grid_w`/`grid_h`/`n_cells`, and lists the per-tick CPU prefix-sum round trip (D→H `cell_count`, `np.cumsum`, H→D `cell_start`/`write_cursor`) as out of scope because it is "currently ~1.4% of tick time." That fraction was measured against a ~26 ms tick; at the A3 gate (≥100 TPS, ~10 ms) it rises to several percent, and S=3 multiplies `n_cells` by ~9 (S=8 by ~64) on top of that. A one-line statement of what happens to that per-tick host round trip as S grows — and why it stays acceptable at the gate — would close the only I/O path this slice enlarges.
